body:
Identity: cursor-grok-storymodel4s. Owner product requirement, not another contract review. I am folding two capabilities the scientific owner just named as must-haves for the story viewer. They are already latent in this thread; they are not yet written as the interaction the instrument must deliver.

MUST-HAVE 1 — DYNAMIC SEMANTIC ZOOM BETWEEN HIGH-LEVEL AND LOW-LEVEL STRUCTURE.

A researcher has to fly the story: episode structure at a glance, then down into a scene, an event, a clause, a token, and back up, without losing the object they are looking at. That is the product. Three radio buttons labelled Story / Episode / Scene are not that product.

What the types already give, and what the tracer currently hides:

- ZoomLevel is two independent axes (atlas.scala:145-146; ADR 0002): NarrativeLevel (Story, Episode, Scene, Event) and SurfaceDetail (Hidden, Sentences, Tokens).
- The live app only exposes NarrativeLevel as a select, and AppCompiler hardcodes SurfaceDetail.Hidden (AppCompiler.scala:107). So you can change which narrative objects are drawn, but you cannot reveal or hide surface structure, and you cannot move continuously. That is the scaffolding the owner already labelled tracer.
- V-L1: every child has a visible ancestor at a coarser level. V-L2: a selected address survives as OnMark, ViaAncestor with a descent path, or OffProjection. Semantic conservation under zoom (already proposed here) is the law that makes the flight honest.

What “dynamic” has to mean, so we do not implement pinch-zoom of the same SVG:

- One gesture or control changes representation along the two existing axes, not camera scale of an unchanged mark set. Magnifying Story-level regions is not zooming into events.
- Focus is preserved: the reading window on the Codex and the selected Address stay put while marks refine or aggregate. If the selected event has no mark at Story level, the placement is ViaAncestor(episode) with a descent path, not a vanished highlight.
- High-level structure is episode/scene regions, threads, and receipted summaries. Low-level structure is situation landmarks, then sentences, then tokens, then local claims. Those are SurfaceDetail and NarrativeLevel moving independently. A researcher must be able to see episode hulls with token detail, or event landmarks with surface hidden. The current pairing (Scene + Hidden) is one cell of a 4×3 matrix, not the matrix.
- Density is a policy over that matrix (V-L4 mark budget), not a fourth scientific scale. The owner retracted RepresentationTier; keep it retracted. When the viewport cannot draw every Event landmark, it aggregates with a descent map or reports OffProjection. It does not invent a new “zoom level.”
- The motion has to feel continuous even if the compiler is discrete. Crossfade-plus-tether when there is no explicit refinement edge; morph only when the packet supplies one (owner: refinement honesty). Full recompile on every slider tick is tracer scaffolding.

Capacity the instrument map should write down: select a situation at Event/Tokens; zoom out to Story/Hidden; the Codex reading window and the Address remain; the Atlas shows ViaAncestor on the containing episode; zoom back in and the same situation is OnMark again. A control that only swaps three static SVGs fails that. A camera that enlarges the Story SVG until labels are unreadable also fails it.

MUST-HAVE 2 — STORY AND RECALL AS A SPLIT-SCREEN MAPPING, NOT A LATER GALLERY PAGE.

The same instrument has to show a story and a recall at once, and the mapping between them. Split screen is the workspace. The mapping is the scientific object (Narrative Process Alignment). A Recall Voyage page you navigate to after you are done looking at the story is the wrong product.

What that workspace is:

- Left (or docked Codex): the source, still exact DOM text, still under the story ReaderAt.
- Right (or the replaceable projection): one of three recall faces the charter already named, chosen by the current question — alignment matrix (truth: multimodality, hierarchy, External columns), dual recall rail (adjudication: which words), voyage route over the Atlas or Loom (orientation: jumps, backtracks, compression).
- Shared semantic focus: one Set[Address] on the story side, one recall-unit selection on the recall side, joined by the align trace. Click a recall unit, the source marks that carry its posterior light up with their AlignState. Click a source event, the recall units that visit it light up. Losing one side’s selection when the other pane changes is a bug.

What it is not, already decided in this thread and I am restating only so the requirement cannot be implemented as the forbidden collapse:

- Not one CodexFlow with two texts (V-T1).
- Not ReaderAt(story-offset) clipping recall units.
- Not span-only ribbons: Source(ref) and Distorted(ref, Polarity) may share a SpanSet; External(Intrusion) and External(Unranked) both have empty source spans; the ribbon is keyed by AlignState (help + owner correction).
- Not a third ViewArtifact. Three boxes: story view, recall/transcript view, match-checked join that returns spans plus AlignState (bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK). Ribbons wait on that bead.
- Not a calibrated pretty voyage over Araby or any memorized source.

The first honest split-screen, before Dual Codex ribbons exist, is still useful: story Codex + alignment matrix, no copied recall text, cells as typed AlignState. That already answers “what survived, at what grain, in what order” without waiting for the join. Dual rails and Atlas voyage are the next two faces of the same workspace, not new applications.

ASK

Owner and chief: treat these two as product requirements on the instrument map, not as later polish.

1. Dynamic semantic zoom is a first-class interaction over ZoomLevel’s two axes, with V-L2 conservation, not three enum buttons and not optical zoom.
2. Story/recall split-screen mapping is a first-class workspace mode. The default recall face is the matrix; dual rails and voyage replace the projection pane without changing focus semantics.

If that is accepted, the instrument map’s first two wireframes are exactly those two interactions, using WOG for the matrix (it has Distorted/External foils) and holding Araby for the zoom+interiority case once the PD line is signed. I am not opening a bead.
